extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and criteria for receiving, evaluating, entering, refusing, and processing amendments filed after allowance (under 37 CFR 1.312) and the use/limits of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (swearing behind).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of amendments under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of 'amendments' by applicant after allowance which must comply with 37 CFR 1.312: (A) an amendment to the specification, (B) a change in the drawings, (C) an amendment to the claims, (D) a change in the inventorship, (E) the submission of prior art, (F) a request to correct the spelling of an inventor's name (37 CFR 1.48(f)), (G) a request to change the order of the names of the inventors (37 CFR 1.48(f)), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amendments must also comply with other applicable requirements (e.g., amendments to specification, drawings, or claims must comply with 37 CFR 1.121 in addition to 1.312; submission of prior art must comply with 1.97 and 1.98 in addition to 1.312).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for filing amendments under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must be filed on or before the date the issue fee is paid, except where the amendment is required by the Office of Data Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.312 does not permit filing an amendment after the issue fee is paid unless the Office of Data Management has delegated authority to accept such amendment (see MPEP § 714.16(d), subsection III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 required
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is non‑compliant under 1.121 and entry would otherwise have been recommended, the amendment and the non-compliance may be corrected using an examiner's amendment. See MPEP § 714 for treatment of non-compliant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner authority after Notice of Allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Allowance is mailed, the application is technically no longer under the jurisdiction of the primary examiner, but the primary examiner can make examiner's amendments and has authority to enter amendments submitted after Notice of Allowance that embody merely the correction of formal matters in the specification or drawing, or formal matters in a claim without changing the scope thereof, or the cancellation of claims, without forwarding to the supervisory patent examiner for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments other than those which merely correct formal matters or cancel claims require approval by the supervisory patent examiner. The TC Director sets policy on trivial informalities that seldom affect disclosure clarity or claim-defining clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for considering amendments under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 cannot be demanded as a matter of right; prosecution should be complete at time of Notice of Allowance. However, amendments may be considered where they are shown (A) to be needed for proper disclosure or protection of the invention, and (B) to require no substantial amount of additional work on the part of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both (A) and (B) are satisfied, the amendment may be considered and, if proper, entry may be recommended by the primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for remarks accompanying substantive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: For amendments affecting the disclosure, the scope of any claim, or that add a claim, the remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state the reasons on which reliance is placed to show: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of 37 CFR 1.111(c) with respect to pointing out the patentable novelty of any claim sought to be added or amended apply in the case of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312, as in ordinary amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.312 not to be used for continued prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was not intended to provide a way for continued prosecution of an application after it has been passed for issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recommendation is against entry, a detailed statement is not necessary; a simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and a brief reason is usually adequate. Sufficient reasons include: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; or (C) the amendment would involve materially added work on the part of the Office (e.g., checking excessive editorial changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copied patent claims and entry rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment received after notice of allowance includes one or more claims copied or substantially copied from a patent, follow MPEP Chapter 2300; the entry of the copied patent claims is not a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.19 for circumstances where copied claims may be refused entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed with motion under 37 CFR 41.208
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed with a motion under 37 CFR 41.208(c)(2) that applies to an application in issue is not entered unless and until the motion has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment adds claims in excess of the number previously paid for, additional fees are required and the amendment is not considered unless accompanied by the full fee required (see MPEP § 607 and 35 U.S.C. 41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and routing of 1.312 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 are sent to the Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) to be scanned and uploaded into the IFW. OPAP messages the Office of Data Management, which reviews and forwards to the Technology Center (TC) which allowed the application. If an amendment was filed directly with the TC, the paper will be forwarded to OPAP for scanning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-delivered amendments under 1.312 are no longer accepted in the TC and may only be delivered to the Customer Service Window listed in MPEP § 501. If the application classification has been transferred to another TC after allowance, the proposed amendment and papers are transmitted to the other TC and the Publishing Division notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner annotation and forwarding for substantive amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 affects the disclosure of the specification, adds claims, or changes the scope of any claim, the examiner must annotate the amendment with 'OK' (recommended for entry), 'Enter In Part' (only part recommended), or 'Do Not Enter' (none recommended), and forward the recommendation to the supervisory patent examiner for consideration and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If favorably considered, it is entered and a Response to Rule 312 Communication (PTO-271) is prepared; primary examiner indicates recommendation by stamping and signing PTO-271; use form paragraphs 7.85 (entered), 7.87 (not entered), or 7.86 (entered in part) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry in part guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: General rule that an amendment should not be entered in part and refused in part should not be relaxed, but where a plurality of claims or claim amendments include some enterable and some not, the acceptable claims or amendments should be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate refused claims using strike-out, renumber claims if necessary to run consecutively, submit PTO-271 recommending entry of acceptable portion and nonentry of remaining portion with reasons, forward to supervisory examiner. Entry-in-part is not recommended unless full additional fee (if any) accompanies the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment filed after period for reply expired
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is not prosecuted within the period set for reply and thereafter an amendment is filed without a petition for extension of time and fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a), such amendment shall be placed in the file but not formally entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff shall immediately notify the applicant by telephone and letter that the amendment was not filed within the time period and therefore cannot be entered and that the application is abandoned unless a petition for extension of time and the appropriate fee are timely filed. See MPEP § 711.02 and § 710.02(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing/inspection of entered amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: After entry of an amendment the application is 'up for action' and forwarded to the examiner, who is responsible for its proper disposal. The examiner should immediately inspect the amendment as set forth in MPEP § 714.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of an amendment after final rejection for compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 should be left to the examiner; technical support staff should not treat such compliance before forwarding the amendment to the examiner. If non-compliant, the examiner should notify applicant and attach a Notice of Non‑Compliant Amendment to the advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — unpatentable claim or new search when prosecution closed
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting an unpatentable claim, or a claim requiring a new search or otherwise raising a new issue in an application whose prosecution before the primary examiner has been closed (e.g., all claims allowed; all claims finally rejected; some claims allowed and remainder finally rejected) is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 714.12–714.14 for exceptions and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — substitute specification noncompliant (37 CFR 1.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute specification that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.125 is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(q) and § 714.20 for substitute specification submission guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — examiner-suggested claim not timely presented
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent claim suggested by the examiner and not presented within the time limit set or an extension thereof is ordinarily denied entry unless entry is authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2300 for policy on such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — copied patent claims conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: While copied patent claims are generally admitted even though the application is under final rejection or on appeal, under certain conditions the claims may be refused entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2300 for conditions when copied claims may be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — unsigned or improperly signed
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsigned or improperly signed amendment or one signed by a suspended or excluded attorney or agent is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper signature and authority before entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — filed after expiration of statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed in the USPTO after the expiration of the statutory period or set time period for reply and any extension thereof is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.17 for handling amendments filed after reply period expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — wording prevents accurate entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment so worded that it cannot be entered with certain accuracy is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714, subsection II.G for examples and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — cancellation of all claims without substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all of the claims and presenting no substitute claim or claims is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.115(b)(1), MPEP § 711.01 and § 714.01(e) regarding abandoned status and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — after notice of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment after a notice of allowance has been mailed in an application is ordinarily denied entry, with certain limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.16 for exceptions (e.g., Office of Data Management required amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — drawings alleged to contain new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the drawing held by the examiner to contain new matter are not entered until the question of new matter is settled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice does not apply to amendments to the specification and claims (which are handled under new matter rules elsewhere, see MPEP § 608.04 et seq.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — objectionable remarks (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks that, in the opinion of the examiner, brings it within the condemnation of 37 CFR 1.3, will be submitted to the Deputy Commissioner for Patents for review and may be denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Deputy Commissioner determines remarks violate 37 CFR 1.3, they will notify the applicant of non-entry of the paper. See MPEP § 714.25 and MPEP § 1002.02(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — cannot be scanned or reproduced
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that cannot be scanned or clearly reproduced are ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.07 for scanning/reproduction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — claims excess of paid number without fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper presenting claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for and not accompanied by the full fee for the claims or authorization to charge the fee is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 509 and § 607 for fee procedures and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — nonresponsive cancellation/election issues
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention should not be entered as it is nonresponsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be notified as directed in MPEP § 714.03 and § 714.05. See MPEP § 821.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment including changes to the specification/claims which is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., one which does not include replacement paragraphs or claim listings) is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714 for examples and procedures for non-compliant amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — preliminary amendment interfering with first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment that unduly interferes with the preparation of a first Office action may be denied entry; factors for denying entry are set forth in 37 CFR 1.115(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of the timing and interference with Office workflow is required; see MPEP § 714.01(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments ordinarily denied entry — supplemental replies outside suspension period
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply is not entered as a matter of right unless it is filed during a suspension period under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2) and MPEP § 714.03(a) for supplemental reply rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments entered in part — substitute specification with other acceptable matter
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'amendment' presenting an unacceptable substitute specification along with amendatory matter (e.g., amendments to claims or new claims) should be entered in part: the substitute specification should be denied entry and so marked, while the rest of the paper should be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry-in-part avoids confusing the record; substitute specifications filed after notice of allowance are not a matter of right. See 37 CFR 1.125 and MPEP § 608.01(q).

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments entered in part — partially approved 1.312 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 which in part is approved and in other part disapproved is entered only as to the approved part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should indicate which parts entered and which not, and supervisory signature required for entry-in-part (see form paragraph 7.86).

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments entered in part — Ex Parte Quayle/closed prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: In an application in which prosecution on the merits is closed (after an Ex Parte Quayle action), where an amendment cures a noted formal defect and adds one or more claims some or all of which are not patentable or will require a further search, the amendment will be entered only as to the formal matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has no right to have new claims considered or entered at this point in the prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments entered in part — amendment accompanying partially granted motion
rubrics_metrics.description: In an amendment accompanying a motion granted only in part, the amendment is entered only to the extent that the motion was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner marks 'Enter' opposite enterable portions using the Stamper tool in Adobe Acrobat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertently entered amendments have no legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If technical support staff inadvertently enters an amendment when it should not have been entered, such entry is of no legal effect; the same action is taken as if the changes had not been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless deleted, annotate the amendatory paper margin with 'Not Officially Entered'. If retained in the file though not entered, give the paper a paper number and list it on the file wrapper with the notation 'Not Entered'. See 37 CFR 1.3 and MPEP § 714.25 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourtesy and 37 CFR 1.3 — non-entry for discourteous remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct business with the USPTO with decorum and courtesy (37 CFR 1.3). Papers presented in violation of this requirement will be submitted to the Director and will not be entered; a notice of non-entry will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discourteous remarks appear, either ignore the discourtesy or submit the paper to the Deputy Commissioner for Patents for review. Complaints against examiners must be made in separate correspondence from other papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 purpose — swearing behind references
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 permits submission of an appropriate oath or declaration to establish invention of the subject matter of a rejected claim prior to the effective date of the reference or activity on which the rejection is based, or to disqualify a commonly owned patent or published application as prior art (e.g., by terminal disclaimer plus declaration under 1.131(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used to 'swear behind' certain references and withdraw the rejection (the rejection is withdrawn, not the reference). See MPEP § 715 for scope and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 evidentiary showing required
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing of facts for an oath or declaration under 1.131(a) shall be such, in character and weight, as to establish reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, or conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to said date to a subsequent reduction to practice or to the filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, must accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration or their absence must be satisfactorily explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and temporal limits for 1.131 swearing behind
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 1.131(a) prior invention may not be established in any country other than the United States, a NAFTA country, or a WTO member country; and prior invention may not be established under 1.131(a) before Dec 8, 1993 in NAFTA countries other than the U.S., or before Jan 1, 1996 in WTO member countries other than NAFTA members (for pre‑AIA cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a country joined the WTO after Jan 1, 1996, the effective date for proving inventive activity in that country for pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 104 and 1.131(a) is the date the country became a WTO member. See MPEP § 213.01 for list of WTO members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 1.131 affidavits/declarations can be used
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 1.131 may be used to overcome rejections in applications subject to pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102, and to overcome rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) in applications subject to pre‑AIA 102 and current 102 in situations such as: (A) to antedate a reference qualifying as prior art under pre‑AIA 102(a) but not under pre‑AIA 102(b) (e.g., prior art date less than 1 year before applicant's effective date); (B) to antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e) where the reference shows but does not claim interfering subject matter; (C) during examination to antedate an activity qualifying as prior art under pre‑AIA 102(g) but not under pre‑AIA 102(b) (e.g., prior art date less than 1 year before applicant's effective date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art is a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that claims interfering subject matter, it may not be antedated under 1.131; see MPEP § 715.05 for interfering subject matter discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 1.131 affidavits/declarations are inappropriate — current 102 or statutory bar
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 1.131(a) is not appropriate where: (A) the application is subject to current 35 U.S.C. 102 and the affidavit is not directed to evidence used in a rejection based on pre‑AIA 102(g); (B) the reference publication date is more than 1 year prior to the effective filing date of the claimed invention (statutory bar under pre‑AIA 102(b)); (C) the reference U.S. patent or application publication claims interfering subject matter as defined in 37 CFR 41.203(a); (D) the reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to the applicant (or legal representatives/assigns) issued prior to the domestic filing date on an application filed more than 12 months prior to the domestic filing date (pre‑AIA 102(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some common‑ownership situations where claims are not identical but not patentably distinct, a terminal disclaimer plus an affidavit under 1.131(c) may be used to overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection; see MPEP § 718.
